hook: A news story says the "average" reaction time in a driving study was 362 milliseconds. But on nine of ten trials the driver reacted in 320 ms or less; one trial was slow because the driver sneezed. Which number describes this driver? Choosing between the mean and the median is a question the exam asks again and again.

prereq.q: Which kind of data is a list of reaction times in milliseconds?
prereq.why: Numbers such as times, scores and counts are quantitative data.

prereq.q: A scatterplot of hours studied against quiz scores shows points rising to the right. What does this show?
prereq.why: Points rising together show a positive correlation, which does not by itself show cause.

figure.caption: In a positively skewed distribution, the mean is pulled toward the tail, past the median (invented data).

chain.cause: Add every value and divide by how many there are
chain.effect: the mean, which uses every value and so moves toward any outlier

chain.cause: Put the values in order and take the middle one (or the average of the two middle ones)
chain.effect: the median, which stays with the typical values even when there are outliers

chain.cause: A few extreme values stretch one side of a distribution
chain.effect: the distribution is skewed and the mean moves toward the tail, so the median is the better summary

chain.cause: Scores sit far from the mean
chain.effect: the range and the standard deviation are large: more variation

ideas: Central tendency: the mean ($\bar{x}$, the total divided by the count), the median (the middle value in order) and the mode (the most frequent value). Two peaks make a bimodal distribution.
An outlier pulls the mean toward it. In a skewed distribution the mean sits toward the tail, so the median describes the typical case better.
Variation: the range is highest minus lowest; the standard deviation is roughly the typical distance of scores from the mean.
A frequency distribution counts how often each value or range occurs; a histogram shows it as touching bars.

misconception.wrong: The mean is always the best "average", and a negative skew means the scores are low.
misconception.right: With outliers or skew, the median is usually the better summary. Skew is named for the tail: a negative skew has a tail toward the low values, often because most scores are high.

summary: Descriptive statistics summarize a set of numbers. The mean, median and mode describe the center; the range and standard deviation describe the spread. Outliers pull the mean toward them, so in a skewed distribution the median is the better summary of a typical value. A frequency distribution or histogram shows the shape: symmetric, skewed toward a tail, or bimodal with two peaks.
